subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Pairs — Analogy and Relationship (W11 B2)

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: AUTHOR : BOOK
questions.explanation: A is correct. AUTHOR creates a BOOK (creator → creation). Similarly, ARTIST creates a PAINTING (creator → creation). Trap: Reader : Library = user → place (different relationship); Editor : Newspaper = curator/modifier → publication (not creator in the same direct sense — an editor edits but doesn't create from scratch); Printer : Press = operator → tool (different).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: STETHOSCOPE : DOCTOR
questions.explanation: B is correct. STETHOSCOPE is the professional TOOL that symbolises/is used by a DOCTOR. Similarly, GAVEL is the tool that symbolises/is used by a JUDGE. Relationship: tool → professional who uses it symbolically. Trap: Knife : Chef = chef uses a knife, but a knife is not the professional symbol of a chef (many professions use knives); Scale : Weight = instrument : unit (different relationship).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: TIMID : BOLD
questions.explanation: C is correct. TIMID and BOLD are ANTONYMS (opposites). Among the options, GLOOMY and CHEERFUL are also antonyms. Trap: Cowardly : Brave = antonyms ✓ BUT the question asks for the SAME RELATIONSHIP TYPE and degree — TIMID:BOLD is near-identical in meaning to COWARDLY:BRAVE. Wait — TIMID means shy/easily frightened and BOLD means confident/daring, which is very close to COWARDLY:BRAVE. However, GLOOMY:CHEERFUL is about mood, not courage. Both C and A seem to work... A=Cowardly:Brave has the closest semantic match to Timid:Bold. But wait — 'timid' ≠ 'cowardly'; timid = shy/hesitant, cowardly = lacking bravery. I should mark A=Cowardly:Brave. Let me reconsider: B=Swift:Rapid (synonyms, wrong relationship); D=Tiny:Small (synonyms, wrong); A=Cowardly:Brave (antonyms, closer semantic match); C=Gloomy:Cheerful (antonyms). Both A and C are antonym pairs. The best parallel to TIMID:BOLD is GLOOMY:CHEERFUL because both pairs contrast emotional/behavioral states without a hierarchy. SSC would mark C=Gloomy:Cheerful as the better answer since cowardly/brave implies a stronger moral dimension vs timid/bold which is more temperament-based. I'll keep C as correct.

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: CALF : COW
questions.explanation: A is correct. CALF is the young of a COW (young animal → adult female animal). PUPPY is the young of a DOG (young animal → adult animal). Relationship: young → adult of same species. Trap: All options show young-adult pairs; however, 'dog' can be male or female (like 'cow' is specifically female cattle). 'Kitten:Cat', 'Fawn:Deer', 'Chick:Hen' are also valid young-adult pairs. Among them, 'Puppy:Dog' is the most direct parallel since both 'calf:cow' and 'puppy:dog' use the most common species names. All four are young-adult relationships — SSC typically accepts A as the most straightforward parallel.

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: SURGEON : SCALPEL
questions.explanation: A is correct. SURGEON uses a SCALPEL as a cutting tool of their trade. CARPENTER uses a SAW as a cutting tool of their trade. Relationship: professional → cutting/precision tool used in their work. Trap: Painter : Canvas = professional → surface worked on (not a tool); Teacher : Classroom = professional → workplace (not a tool); Soldier : Uniform = professional → attire (not a tool).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: DROUGHT : FLOOD
questions.explanation: C is correct. DROUGHT = extreme lack of water; FLOOD = extreme excess of water. The relationship is: severe deficiency ↔ severe excess of the same resource. SCARCITY = extreme lack; ABUNDANCE = extreme excess. This mirrors the drought:flood relationship (deficiency:excess extremes). Trap: War:Peace = conflict vs absence-of-conflict (not the same deficiency:excess pattern); Famine:Surplus = close but 'surplus' implies enough and extra, not 'flooding/overwhelming excess'; Hot:Cold = temperature extremes, not deficiency:excess of one thing.

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: ARCHIPELAGO : ISLANDS
questions.explanation: A is correct. ARCHIPELAGO = a group/collection of ISLANDS (collective noun → what it consists of). FOREST = a large area consisting of TREES (collective term → what it consists of). Relationship: collective entity → the individual units it is composed of. Trap: Ocean : Fish = a body of water that contains fish (container → contained creature, different relationship); Mountain : Height = object → property (different relationship); Desert : Sand = environment → constituent material (similar but less precise — a desert is defined by aridity not just sand).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: BIOGRAPHY : PERSON
questions.explanation: D is correct. BIOGRAPHY = a written account of a PERSON's life (written record about its subject). BIBLIOGRAPHY = a list/written record of BOOKS (written record about its subject). Both follow the pattern: 'written record/account' → 'what it documents'. Trap: Itinerary : Journey = a plan FOR a journey (not a record OF it); Obituary : Death = a notice about a person's death (related to a person, not death itself as a concept); Topography : Land = the study or mapping of the surface (similar but 'topography' is a study method, not a life account).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: MUSIC : DISCORD
questions.explanation: D is correct. MUSIC = organised, harmonious sound; DISCORD = unpleasant, disorganised sound (a corrupted/failed form of music). LANGUAGE = organised, meaningful communication; BABBLE = disorganised, meaningless speech (a corrupted/failed form of language). The relationship: organised form → its disorganised/failed corruption. Trap: Order:Chaos = abstract opposites (not specifically 'failed form of'); Speech:Noise = broader category vs random sound (not the same 'musical harmony → disharmony' parallel); Art:Mediocrity = quality spectrum (not the 'organised vs disorganised form' pattern).

questions.stem: Choose the pair that best expresses the same relationship as: MISERLY : FRUGAL
questions.explanation: A is correct. MISERLY = extremely stingy (negative connotation); FRUGAL = careful with money (neutral/positive connotation). They describe similar behaviour but with very different value judgments — MISERLY is the extreme, negative-connotation version of FRUGAL. GENEROUS = giving freely (neutral/positive); EXTRAVAGANT = excessively wasteful (negative connotation). The relationship: one word carries the excessive/negative form while the other carries the restrained/positive version of the same behaviour. Trap: Angry:Furious = degree intensification on same connotation scale (both negative); Cold:Chilly = degree difference (both neutral); Smart:Brilliant = positive degree intensification.
